label: prf:quantum-peter-weyl
title: Proof of quantum peter weyl
html:
Proof.

Step 1: Orthogonality (a). The Frobenius form \int_A induces, via the snake identities (pairing_snake_left, pairing_snake_right), a categorical trace \mathrm{tr}_A(f) = \int_A \circ f. The matrix coefficient D^j_{mn} is the (m,n) entry of the representation morphism \rho_j \colon A \to \mathrm{End}(V_j).

By Schur's lemma in \mathbf{C} (which holds because the V_j are simple objects): \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(V_j, V_{j'}) = 0 for j \neq j'. Composing with the Frobenius trace:

  \int_A (D^j_{mn})^\dagger \cdot D^{j'}_{m'n'}
  = \mathrm{tr}_A(\rho_j(e^j_m, e^j_n)^\dagger \circ
    \rho_{j'}(e^{j'}_{m'}, e^{j'}_{n'}))
  = \frac{\delta_{jj'}\delta_{mm'}\delta_{nn'}}
    {\mathrm{tr}_A(\mathrm{id}_{V_j})}

and \mathrm{tr}_A(\mathrm{id}_{V_j}) = [2j+1]_q (quantum dimension from the Pawlowski--Leitner norm).

The result uses only Schur's lemma (which holds in any semisimple abelian category) and the Frobenius trace.

Step 2: Completeness (b). We use the Tannaka--Krein reconstruction. The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-Mod} is faithful and exact (axiom of QOU). By the Tannaka--Krein theorem, A is recovered as the algebra of matrix coefficients:

  A  \cong  \bigoplus_{j \geq 0}
  \mathrm{End}(\tau(V_j))
   \cong 
  \bigoplus_{j \geq 0}
  \mathrm{span}\{D^j_{mn} : -j \leq m,n \leq j\}.

The isomorphism is algebraic — the matrix coefficients span A as a vector space. Since A is dense in L^2(A) (by definition of the Hilbert completion), the matrix coefficients are total in L^2(A). Combined with orthogonality (a), they form a complete orthonormal system.

The argument uses the Tannaka--Krein theorem, which is part of the QOU axioms (the existence of \tau).

Step 3: Eigendecomposition (c). The q-Laplacian \Delta_q = d_q\delta_q + \delta_q d_q commutes with the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) action (because d_q is equivariant and \delta_q is its adjoint). By Schur's lemma, \Delta_q acts as a scalar on each isotypic component \mathrm{End}(V_j). The scalar is the q-Casimir eigenvalue [j]_q[j+1]_q, which is computed from the q-angular momentum structure:

  \Delta_q|_{V_j} = C_q(j) \cdot \mathrm{id}_{V_j},
  \qquad
  C_q(j) = [j]_q[j+1]_q.

The eigenvalue identity follows from equivariance of d_q, Schur's lemma, and the Casimir computation.
